description: Being noticed (stage E step 15): the test yard at night (a lighting override), the night patrol's two guards walking their loop round a lamp post and a low wall, 18 box-body watchers in two rows either side of the loop (some facing it, some away; with the yard's own 14 watchers, 32: 05's cap on NPCs at full detail), and the player walking crouched to and fro through the loop, beside the wall and under the lamp. Measures the detection pass (detection: every watcher's checks every 0.2 s within 30 m of the player and every 0.5 s further out, within a 0.5 ms a frame budget, the nearest first: the sight range from the light at the player, the view cone, up to three rays, the meters; physics time) and the markers above the noticing NPCs (stealth_markers: the pooled slots and their Dear ImGui windows, scripts' time); the patrol's walk is its own stopwatch and switch (patrol: with it off the two guards stand at their start corners and still watch; they are in the picture, so it is a visible switch too). The detection budget is kept per drawn frame (all its physics steps together); CombatGroups' looks in a fight (Detection.sees(), once a second) count in that budget but their time is in combat_ai's stopwatch (combat_ai.groups); no fight runs in this scenario. With detection off nobody notices anything, so no marker fills either: its saving is an upper bound (the pass plus the markers' filling). The scenario's own check (CHECK lines) says the work really ran (checks, looks, rays, markers) or, with a switch off, that it stopped. The markers change the picture, so stealth_markers is a visible switch. Stage E step 16 adds noise inside the detection pass and its stopwatch (the footsteps of the player and the guards, louder on the patrol's wooden boards which the walk crosses, hearing them, the searches with their sight maps, the sneak uses): the switch noise (with it off no noise is made or heard and nobody searches; seeing is as in step 15). With it off the guards don't turn or search, and no marker fills from hearing, so it changes the picture: it is a visible switch too. The yard gained a table with a crate and wooden boards west of the loop, so the baseline must be recorded again. Records its own baseline the first time it runs; run it on this PC and on the laptop (its Intel graphics at low), and npc_crowd once.
